description: Unauthorized Access to Media Content via S3 Bucket Misconfiguration Misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or improperly scoped CloudFront OAC settings could create paths for unauthorized access to media content. The complexity of IAM roles in the architecture (multiple service roles interacting with S3) increases the risk of misconfiguration. An attacker with access to an overly permissive IAM role (e.g., through a compromised Lambda function) could directly access S3 buckets, bypassing CloudFront and authentication controls.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policies using least privilege principle
recommendation: Implement comprehensive S3 access logging and monitoring

description: Insufficient Audit Logging for User Actions and API Access While CloudWatch logging is configured, potential gaps exist in logging coverage, log retention policies, and log protection mechanisms. This could allow attackers to perform actions without detection or tamper with logs to hide their activities. An attacker gains access through a compromised user account and performs unauthorized content access or modifications. Without comprehensive logging, their actions may go undetected or be difficult to trace during incident response.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1562.001 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
recommendation: Implement comprehensive logging strategy across all components
recommendation: Implement log protection and centralized log analysis

description: Insufficient Data Encryption at Rest The architecture uses S3-managed encryption (SSE-S3) by default instead of KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for some components. This limits the ability to audit key usage and control key rotation policies. An attacker with physical access to storage media or with elevated AWS permissions could potentially access data without going through application-level controls if KMS encryption is not used.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
recommendation: Implement KMS encryption across all data stores
recommendation: Implement strict key usage policies and monitoring

description: GraphQL API Security Vulnerabilities GraphQL APIs can be vulnerable to complex queries that cause excessive resource consumption, field-level authorization bypass, and injection attacks through resolver mapping templates. An attacker crafts a deeply nested GraphQL query that causes high CPU usage in the Lambda resolver, or attempts to access unauthorized fields through carefully crafted queries.
references: recommendation: Implement comprehensive AppSync API security controls
recommendation: Secure Lambda resolvers and implement monitoring

description: Media Processing Pipeline Vulnerabilities The media processing pipeline involves multiple services handling live and VOD content. Misconfiguration of input security groups, encryption settings, or access controls could allow unauthorized access or manipulation of media streams. An attacker could attempt to hijack live streams by exploiting misconfigured MediaLive input security groups, or inject unauthorized content through unprotected MediaConnect flows.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Secure media input and processing pipeline
recommendation: Implement comprehensive monitoring and alerting
